findings.title: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without cacheMu while BuildIndex now writes it under a narrower lock
findings.body: `TotalDocs` ranges over `b.cache` with no lock. This PR adds a call to it in `searchSupport.init` (search.go:216) and moves `cacheMu` in `BuildIndex` to cover only the map write (137-139). If any index build or event-driven index creation runs concurrently with this call, or with the metrics collector at bleve_index_metrics.go:96, the result is a concurrent map read and write, which can crash the process with a fatal error. Take `cacheMu.RLock()` in `TotalDocs`.

findings.title: Init moved into the constructor; Stop's initErr no longer gates requests
findings.body: `Init` now runs in `NewResourceServer`, so the constructor blocks on the full search index build and fails if it fails. That is the intent, but the `s.Init(ctx)` check was also removed from every RPC handler. `Stop` sets `s.initErr = "service is stopping"` (line 321), and that value is no longer returned to callers of Create, Update, Delete, Read and the other handlers. Requests during shutdown now go to the backend. Check that this is acceptable, or add an explicit stopping check.

findings.title: Test skipped for postgres and reordering of init/watcher has no new coverage
findings.body: The postgres skip in module_server_test.go is a workaround with no linked issue. The change that moves search init before the watcher and runs `Init` eagerly in the constructor is not covered by any new test.

summary: Moving Init into the constructor looks intentional. I found one likely data race: `bleveBackend.TotalDocs` reads the index cache without a lock, and this PR adds a call to it and narrows the lock in `BuildIndex`. I also noted that `Stop`'s "service is stopping" error no longer reaches callers, and that the reordering has no new test coverage.
